analysis:
Examined SSDPrefixCache.swift BASE lines 657–1836 and the complete eviction patch. The sole mapped change replaces the bounded victim loop at BASE 1772–1786 with SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest, retaining hasSafeRoot, retireIndexedEntries, and positive-byte eviction accounting. No independently supported regression can be established without the new helper's implementation. Integration must verify that delegation preserves bounded traversal, skips undeletable victims, stops on externalChange, and returns indexed bytes actually freed; these contracts affect T-041's box-wide LRU budget and availability under adversarial storage.
Surrounding donation code preserves adoption/benefit and staging-size gates, salt-scoped HMAC tags, bounded write-behind submission, endurance checks, and sidecar context commitments (BASE 862–1124, 1149–1245). Staging retains epoch checks, bounded authenticated reads with model/layout/tag bindings, cancellation cleanup, shared reservation accounting, and recompute/replay fallback (BASE 1290–1691). Ticket release and retirement interactions remain visible at BASE 1722–1808: deletion is serialized with removalLock and guarded by safe-root/ownership checks, while external changes trigger reconciliation. These unchanged controls are context, not newly audited guarantees. No changed authorization, attestation, wire encryption, billing, or plaintext exposure behavior appears in these units. Remaining material uncertainty is the delegated eviction algorithm; review SSDOwnedEntryRetirement and its callers/tests in integration before concluding that disk-budget enforcement is preserved.
